title: Super law rule summary — Conditions of release & preservation (FY2026-27)
summary: When preserved super can be paid out, based on Schedule 1 of the SIS Regulations as applied by Caldova. A member's benefit is made up of preserved, restricted non-preserved and unrestricted non-preserved amounts; preserved and restricted amounts can only be cashed when a condition of release is met, and then only up to that condition's cashing restriction. Preservation age is 60 for everyone born after 30 June 1964, so in 2026-27 it is effectively 60 for all members. Benefits & Eligibility use this summary to decide whether a withdrawal, pension commencement or early release can proceed; Onboarding uses it to check the request type and evidence.
rules:
Conditions of release (cashing restriction in brackets):
1 Retirement after reaching preservation age — members aged 60–64 give a written declaration that an employment arrangement has ended and they never intend to work 10 or more hours a week again (nil).
2 Ceasing an employment arrangement on or after age 60 (nil for amounts accrued up to that point).
3 Reaching age 65 — no retirement or work test; the whole balance becomes unrestricted non-preserved (nil).
4 Transition to retirement — from preservation age while still working, as a non-commutable income stream paying between 4% and 10% of the balance each year (restricted).
5 Death (nil) — paid as a death benefit under the trust deed.
6 Permanent incapacity (nil).
7 Temporary incapacity — non-commutable income stream for the period of incapacity, usually from insured income protection.
8 Terminal medical condition — two registered medical practitioners, at least one a specialist, certify an illness likely to result in death within 24 months; lump sums are tax-free (nil).
9 Severe financial hardship — 26 continuous weeks of eligible Commonwealth income support and unable to meet reasonable and immediate family living expenses: one lump sum of $1,000–$10,000 in any 12 months, applied for through the fund (see the severe financial hardship rule summary).
10 Compassionate grounds — medical treatment or medical transport, home or vehicle modifications for a severe disability, palliative care, funeral costs for a dependant, or preventing foreclosure of a mortgage or forced sale of the home. Approved by the ATO, not the fund; the fund pays the amount the ATO approves.
11 Other ATO-authorised releases — e.g. First Home Super Saver releases, and release authorities for contributions over the caps or for Division 293 tax.
Unrestricted non-preserved amounts can be paid at any time. Rollovers between complying funds are not cash payments and do not need a condition of release — preserved money stays preserved in the receiving fund.
limits: Preserved super cannot be released to pay debts (other than through the hardship or compassionate grounds rules), to buy a home (outside the First Home Super Saver scheme) or simply because the member needs money. Promoters who offer early access through an SMSF are operating illegally — amounts released illegally are taxed at the member's marginal rate and penalties can apply. A transition-to-retirement income stream cannot be cashed as a lump sum (except unrestricted amounts) and its earnings are taxed in the fund until the member retires or turns 65. Evidence is required for every condition; Caldova never relies on a verbal statement.
evidenceRequired: Proof of age (identity verified at onboarding)
Retirement declaration (members aged 60–64 relying on retirement)
Medical certificates — two practitioners including a specialist (terminal medical condition) or permanent incapacity certification
Services Australia confirmation letter dated within 21 days plus statutory declaration (severe financial hardship)
ATO approval letter or release authority (compassionate grounds, First Home Super Saver, contributions over the caps, Division 293)
